meeting_header:
Date: 2026-05-07 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Nina Patel (AtlasCare ML Lead), Carlos Ramirez (AtlasCare Platform Eng), Dr. Ellen Yu (AtlasCare CTO)
summary: Intro demo of Redwood Optimize console QProfile workflow, discussion of INT8 vs FP8 tradeoffs for AtlasCare inference use (clinical summarization), initial pilot plan and next steps (sandbox, benchmarks, compliance docs).
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll run about 45 minutes, quick agenda: console tour, QProfile concept, live demo with sample prompts, then pilot next steps.
[00:00:18] Nina Patel: Thanks Maya, appreciate it. Quick context - we're trying to push clinical note summarization in production, latency SLO around 150ms p95, cost is a big factor.
[00:00:34] Liam O'Connor: Great, and hi all; I'll jump into the console demo and the quantization profiles — show how we pick INT8 vs FP8 depending on fidelity.
[00:00:47] Carlos Ramirez: One ask up front - we need to keep everything in our VPC for PHI; what does Redwood Private look like here?
[00:00:59] Maya Chen: We'll cover compliance later; short answer: Private + KMS + audit logs are available. I'll send the SOC2/KMS doc after.
[00:01:10] Dr. Ellen Yu: Also curious — do you have runway for burst capacity? Our load spikes during morning huddles.
[00:01:18] Liam O'Connor: Yes we can allocate dedicated pools and burst to hosted if you allow hybrid; we'll show autoscale config in the console.
[00:01:30] [00:01:30] Liam O'Connor: Okay screen share — opening Redwood Optimize console. First panel is model catalog, then Optimize -> QProfiles. Here we run a profile generation job that samples prompts and measures quality deltas across precision tiers.
[00:01:51] Liam O'Connor: For this demo I uploaded a small sample set of AtlasCare prompts (thanks Carlos). We'll run a quick quant sweep: fp16 baseline, int8, and fp8.
[00:02:06] Nina Patel: Quick clarification — is FP8 a Redwood thing or model-specific? Our data ops team is worried about unsupported kernels.
[00:02:16] Liam O'Connor: FP8 depends on model and kernel support; Redwood's runtime supports multiple FP8 backends and will pick kernels at compile time. Sometimes the fallback will choose INT8 if FP8 is unsupported for a particular op.
[00:02:34] [00:02:34] Maya Chen: We also surfaced a compatibility column in the QProfile results — shows where fp8 had full coverage vs partial.
[00:02:43] Carlos Ramirez: Cool. Can you show latency numbers? We need concrete p95 figures.
[00:02:49] Liam O'Connor: Yes. Running the sweep now — it's a short run, should take a minute.
[00:02:59] [00:02:59] *brief pause in audio, typing*
[00:03:10] Liam O'Connor: First row is our baseline fp16 tokens per second; p95 ~ 210ms for these prompts on the gpus I'm using in the sandbox (note: sandbox hw ~ A10x vs your prod A100s). INT8 run — p95 drops to ~85-95ms, throughput up ~2.3x. FP8 shows p95 ~75-90ms but some prompts show quality drift on clinical abbreviations.
[00:03:39] Nina Patel: When you say 'quality drift' what metric are you using? ROUGE? Clinical entity F1?
[00:03:47] Liam O'Connor: For this sample job we used a mixed metric: BLEU/ROUGE for surface similarity and an entity-level recall check for critical clinical terms. The Optimize console lets you plug in custom evaluators — you can upload your own scorer to emphasize entity recall.
[00:04:02] Dr. Ellen Yu: Our priority is preserving critical terms (medications, dosages). If FP8 drops entity recall at all that's a non-starter.
[00:04:11] Liam O'Connor: Totally. The console flags any profile where entity recall delta > threshold (we default to 1% absolute). In this run, FP8 had a 0.8% drop average but the worst-case prompt had a 2.3% drop — that's why we show a per-prompt heatmap.
[00:04:29] Carlos Ramirez: Can we do a hybrid route - use FP8 for generic summaries but route flagged prompts to INT8 or full precision?
[00:04:36] Maya Chen: Exactly, that's one of the recommended rollout patterns. Redwood's smart routing can tag by prompt classifier or by regex on output size and route to a higher-fidelity profile when needed.
[00:04:47] [00:04:47] Liam O'Connor: Showing the heatmap now — color-coded by entity recall delta. See these two prompts around medication lists — FP8 dips below our 95% recall threshold.
[00:05:00] Nina Patel: Hmm okay. If we tune FP8 quantization parameters (per-layer tweaks) could that bring those two prompts back?
[00:05:09] Liam O'Connor: Yes, QProfile tuning can target per-layer sensitivity. The console exposes a guided heuristic; you can also run an automated per-layer sensitivity sweep. That often recovers edge-case prompts while preserving the global latency wins.
[00:05:22] Dr. Ellen Yu: What's the risk if we push FP8 to production then roll back? Any cache or session issues?
[00:05:29] Liam O'Connor: We have canary rollouts plus automatic fallback. If quality regression is detected by your eval hooks, Redwood can instant-failover to a nominated profile. KV cache is keyed by profile version so we avoid cross-profile cache pollution.
[00:05:44] Carlos Ramirez: You said KV cache — we've had it called K-V cash in other notes, ha. What happens to latency during a failover?
[00:05:52] Liam O'Connor: There's a small spike as new workers warm up and KV cache warms, typically single-digit percent for p95. That's why we recommend a warm-up window and holdback capacity during rollout.
[00:06:07] [00:06:07] Maya Chen: Quick pause — Nina, do you have an internal latency target for the pilot? You earlier mentioned 150ms p95, is that firm?
[00:06:15] Nina Patel: That's our target for interactive UI. For batch background jobs we can tolerate up to 400ms. Our primary concern is PHI safety.
[00:06:25] Liam O'Connor: Good — that helps. For interactive path FP8 meets 150ms comfortably on dedicated A100 pools per our benchmarks, but we'll validate with your full prompt set.
[00:06:36] [00:06:36] *typing*
[00:06:42] Liam O'Connor: I'm going to open the rollout config — here you can define baseline profile, canary percent, fallback thresholds (quality delta %, latency SLO breaches), and autoscale buffer. For AtlasCare I'd recommend: 5% canary, 10% buffer, entity-recall threshold 1%.
[00:06:59] Carlos Ramirez: What about data residency? We need processing to happen in our region and logs to be retained for 365 days.
[00:07:06] Maya Chen: Private deployment supports region pinning and configurable audit-log retention. We'll include retention settings in the pilot proposal.
[00:07:15] Nina Patel: Pricing — how much difference between INT8 and FP8 per token?
[00:07:21] Maya Chen: Cost delta depends on throughput and sequence length but generally FP8 yields ~15-25% cheaper compute per token vs INT8 because of higher throughput on some kernels; the console also shows estimated unit cost in the profile results. We'll share a pilot pricing sheet.
[00:07:36] [00:07:36] Dr. Ellen Yu: Can you show me the QProfile JSON or manifest? We need to check it against our change control.
[00:07:42] Liam O'Connor: Sure — here's an exported profile manifest. It's human-readable: per-layer precision, fallback rules, seed prompts, evaluator config, and rollout policy.
[00:07:55] Nina Patel: That manifest will help us with the validation checklist. Can the evaluator tie into our internal test harness?
[00:08:02] Liam O'Connor: Yes, you can upload a custom scorer or call a webhook so your harness runs test cases and returns pass/fail metrics to the console.
[00:08:11] Carlos Ramirez: About the hardware — you mentioned the sandbox runs on A10x; our prod is A100s. Will results transfer?
[00:08:19] Liam O'Connor: Kernel performance differs but the Optimize console gives normalized delta estimates and a confidence band. We'll run pilot benchmarks on your target infra as part of the proof.
[00:08:30] [00:08:30] Maya Chen: Quick note — we did a pilot with another health customer where a per-layer tweak in FP8 recovered medication entity recall to parity while maintaining 30% cost savings. So it's feasible, but test-driven.
[00:08:44] Nina Patel: Nice. Ok, for next steps we want the sandbox, the manifest and the SOC2/KMS docs, and then schedule the quant sweep.
[00:08:53] Maya Chen: Got it. We'll share a sandbox link (read-only + test creds), QProfile template, and compliance pack. Liam will run the initial benchmark and upload results.
[00:09:03] Dr. Ellen Yu: Timeline — when can we start the sweep?
[00:09:06] Liam O'Connor: If you share the sample prompts by Friday (2026-05-08), we can run the initial job and have results by 2026-05-14.
[00:09:15] Carlos Ramirez: I can extract and share a 500-prompt subset with edge cases by EOD tomorrow.
[00:09:20] [00:09:20] Nina Patel: One more question — do you do any differential privacy or masking for logs when running in hosted mode?
[00:09:28] Maya Chen: In hosted we support transcript redaction and PII masking hooks; in Private you control the logs. We'll include options in the compliance doc.
[00:09:37] Liam O'Connor: Back to the console — showing the per-prompt drift table and the suggested per-layer tweaks. You can accept suggestions and queue a rerun with modified profile.
[00:09:49] Nina Patel: If we accept a tweak and rerun, does that create a new profile version?
[00:09:54] Liam O'Connor: Yes, versioned profiles, immutable manifests. Rollouts reference a profile ID.
[00:09:59] [00:09:59] Maya Chen: Ok wrapping up — recap of agreed next steps: Maya to send sandbox link + compliance pack by Monday 2026-05-10, Carlos to deliver prompts 2026-05-08, Liam to run benchmarks and share CSV by 2026-05-14, schedule quant sweep session week of 2026-05-18.
[00:10:18] Dr. Ellen Yu: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[00:10:21] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links.
[00:10:26] *call ends*
